title_candidates: Turn AI-made SVGs into shareable images in your browser
A browser tool for sharing AI-made SVGs
summary: Simon Willison upgraded a free browser tool that renders Markdown with SVG graphics and exports shareable PNG, JPEG, or MP4 files.

primary_source.title: Markdown SVG upgrades
primary_source.author: Simon Willison
key_facts: The browser tool renders pasted Markdown that contains SVG graphics.
It can also load Markdown from a CORS-enabled URL or GitHub Gist and create a bookmarkable renderer link.
Readers can copy or download PNG and JPEG versions produced in the browser.
A new MP4 tab appears for animated SVGs and converts them in the browser using ffmpeg.wasm.
The MP4 conversion downloads more than 30 MB of browser code and estimates an animation's loop duration before rendering frames.

quote_candidates.text: The URL option will give you a bookmarkable page

supporting_sources.title: Markdown SVG Renderer
key_facts: The live tool provides Paste and URL inputs, a rendered preview, and export tabs for SVG blocks.

supporting_sources.title: Tools colophon: markdown-svg-renderer
key_facts: The public development log labels the tool AI generated and links the AI-assisted implementation history for its renderer, export features, and security fixes.

prerequisites: Access to an AI assistant that can draft SVG code

steps.instruction: Open https://tools.simonwillison.net/markdown-svg-renderer and confirm Paste is selected, with a Markdown editor on the left and Preview on the right.
Ask an AI assistant: `Return only a fenced svg block for a 600x300 blue card that says TEST in white.` Paste the response into the editor and check that Preview shows the card instead of raw code.
Select the PNG tab above the graphic, wait for the converted preview and file size, then choose Download PNG and open the saved image.
Compare the download with the rendered SVG for clipped labels, missing fonts, or unreadable contrast; revise the SVG source and export again if needed.
Use MP4 only when the SVG is animated and you are willing to download the roughly 31 MB conversion component; verify the video loop before sharing it.

risk_flags: The guide uses non-sensitive content on a third-party page even though rendering and export happen in the browser.
The MP4 path downloads a large WebAssembly dependency and should be skipped on limited connections.
The live output still needs visual inspection before it is shared.
